solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flock of black sheep, small for area

indicators.note: 'small for area' means the abbreviation for small takes the place of the abbreviation for area

blocks.note: a black sheep is an outcast, a pariah
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A shepherd notices one disreputable sheep in the flock and swaps it for a smaller animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in PARIAH (the second one) becomes S, giving PARISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the congregation in a priest's care, which church language calls his flock.

clue.text: Lions intruded, escaping from trap

indicators.note: breaking out of a trap means the letters scramble free into a new order

blocks.note: to pry into something is to intrude, so intruded is pried

explanation.surface: Lions forced their way in, then escaped from a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for a group of lions.

clue.text: Venomous type of gossip blowing top

indicators.note: to blow one's top is to lose the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a prattler chatters idly, a gossip

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venomous type' reads as a nasty person; it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is short for rattlesnake, a poisonous snake.

clue.text: Liberal refused to throttle vacuous lefty, surprisingly

indicators.note: something refused is turned away, so that letter is left out of the next word
vacuous means empty, so the word's insides are dropped and only its outside kept

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
to throttle is to strangle
the outer letters of lefty

explanation.surface: A Liberal oddly declined to silence an empty-headed left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: One L is dropped from STRANGLE, leaving STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely and surprisingly are both adverbs meaning in an unexpected way.

clue.text: Have enough to buy part of Staffordshire

indicators.note: only a part of the next word is wanted, a run of letters lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the county name

explanation.surface: Someone can only afford a modest piece of land in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have the money needed for its purchase.

clue.text: In favour of former currency market

blocks.note: if you are for something you are in favour of it
ex means former

explanation.surface: Someone backs the currency that used to be in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Forex, short for foreign exchange, is the global market where currencies are traded.

clue.text: University dons stole rubbish and left best in shop

indicators.note: rubbish means poor, worthless, so the preceding word is broken up and reformed
to don is to put on, so one piece is wrapped by another like a garment

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: College tutors pinch some junk and walk off.
explanation.walkthrough: University dons are tutors in the surface, but here dons is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsell a rival is to beat them in sales, to be best in the shop.

clue.text: Payment is absurdly curtailed abroad

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off
abroad here means widely scattered, so the letters spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A payment is cut back ridiculously when made overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: ABSURDLY loses its final Y before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A disbursal is a paying out of money, a payment from a fund.

clue.text: Flighty boomer is resentful and close to meltdown

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a synonym: someone resentful is bitter
the final letter of meltdown

explanation.surface: An angry baby boomer sulks as an economic meltdown approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boomer' suggests a baby boomer, but it is a bird known for its booming call; 'flighty' just says it flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a marsh heron whose deep booming call is its best-known feature.

clue.text: Harry Potter's complaint

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or pester, so these letters are knocked about into a new order

blocks.note: the name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: The boy wizard Harry Potter lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous name hides the anagram signal: 'Harry' is a verb here, not the wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a formal objection, a statement of grievance or complaint.

clue.text: Severe European taking part in group sex

indicators.note: to take part in something is to be inside it, so one letter goes within the word

blocks.note: swinging is partner-swapping or group sex
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A stern European joins in an orgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing means severe, especially of cuts or penalties; it is a mainly British word.

clue.text: Spooner's trundling bags closer

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words wanted trade their first sounds

blocks.note: trundling something along is wheeling it; it gives its W sound to the second word
bags are sacks; the S sound moves to the first word

explanation.surface: Spooner pushes his luggage along on a trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheeling sacks, with first sounds swapped, comes out as sealing wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax was used to fasten letters shut, so it is something that closes them.

clue.text: Bamboozle wingless, flightless birds

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two sides, so without them its outer letters go

blocks.note: to bamboozle is to confuse or bemuse

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer is baffled by birds that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: BEMUSE loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly, so emus are an example of flightless birds.

clue.text: Bottle opener, veneered in part

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A wine-bottle opener with a decorative wooden veneer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'bottle' means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and nerve is a synonym for the same quality.

clue.text: Northern man spending pounds for close shave

indicators.note: spending means paying out, so that item is given up from the word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
a human being, an earthling
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling

explanation.surface: A northerner pays a barber to give him a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: The L in EARTHLING goes, leaving EARTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, as is a close shave.

clue.text: Disorder unloosed, with knobs on

indicators.note: disorder puts the following letters out of their proper sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks loose, and in an especially intense form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With knobs on' is a British idiom for 'and even more so', which hides its literal sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulose is a botanical term for bearing small knobby lumps, or nodules.

clue.text: Piqued at heart, embraced by a gender-bending transvestite

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are taken
something embraced is held inside, so it goes within the other piece
bending twists something out of shape, so the letters before it are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle two letters of piqued

explanation.surface: Someone flouting gender norms is privately irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gender-bending' reads as one adjective, but it splits into the letters to shuffle and the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag queen is a man performing in exaggerated female dress, broadly a cross-dresser.

clue.text: Grotesque outburst over drunken orgy

indicators.note: something drunken staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order
one word lying over another covers it, so the outer piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a gale of laughter is an outburst
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone erupts in anger over a debauched drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grotesque' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun for a carved figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque, a monstrous stone figure on a building.

clue.text: Think hosts extremely trivial and weak

indicators.note: at the extremes means at each end, so only the first and last letters are taken
a host holds guests inside, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: to guess is to think, as in 'I guess so'
the first and last letters of trivial

explanation.surface: A dinner host is thought shallow and spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutless means lacking courage, cowardly and weak-willed.

clue.text: Obsessive about new yearly record

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: informally, an obsessively fussy person is anal
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on a fresh annual record.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a chronicle of one year's events, a record kept year by year.

clue.text: Falls over backwards and starts to resent ageing

indicators.note: backwards tells you to read the preceding word from end to start
the starts of the words that follow are their first letters

blocks.note: to do something over is to do it again
the first letters of resent and ageing

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles over backwards and begins to resent growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb, but it means waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, often called Niagara Falls.

clue.text: Tantrists regularly having sex

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Followers of Tantra make love on a frequent schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Tantrists practise Tantra, popularly linked with sex.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At it' is a British euphemism for engaged in intercourse.

clue.text: Must function untiringly at first to stop conspiracy theory

indicators.note: only the first letter of the preceding word is taken
to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: sine is a trigonometric function
QAnon is a far-right American conspiracy theory
the first letter of untiringly

explanation.surface: Tireless effort is needed to halt the spread of a conspiracy theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'without which not', the phrase names an essential condition, a must.

clue.text: Scoundrel wins cycling race at last

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter moves round to the front
at last means at the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of race

explanation.surface: A villain triumphs in a bicycle race in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A swine is a contemptible person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Over-long remark

definitions.note: a verb here: to state as an opinion

blocks.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
to long for something is to pine

explanation.surface: A comment goes on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over-long' reads as one adjective; split it into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, to remark.

clue.text: Family relative behind leader of environmental movement

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
behind places the relative after the piece that follows it in the clue, fixing the order

blocks.note: kin are one's family
the first letter of environmental
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: Someone's relation is behind a green campaign group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the relative after the leader letter. 'Environmental movement' looks like one phrase; only 'movement' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinesis is the scientific term for motion, especially an organism's undirected movement.

clue.text: Top beer brought back for Top Gear

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A first-class beer is brought back for the TV car show Top Gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a British TV motoring show; here it means finery worn on top, such as a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are royal emblems such as crowns, so ceremonial gear including headgear.

clue.text: Good escort is exceptionally effusive person

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: A capable escort turns out to be a wonderfully warm companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is someone who praises in an overflowing, over-enthusiastic way.

clue.text: Clueless Keynesian acting crazy

indicators.note: without a clue, read as without a word meaning clue, which is taken away
acting means playing a part, so the remaining letters perform in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An economist of the Keynes school behaves foolishly, without any idea what he is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: A key is a clue to a puzzle, so KEY is removed from KEYNESIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane and crazy are synonyms for mad or wildly unreasonable.
